edges.description: Grains are carried out of the lesion through the draining sinuses, which discharge them; the grains do not themselves open the sinuses.
Granulomatous tissue becomes surrounded by fibrous tissue.
Neutrophil accumulation and enzyme release digest the subcutaneous tissue, leading to sinus formation.
Digestion of the subcutaneous tissue by the neutrophil and enzyme response produces fluid that causes the tumour-like subcutaneous swelling, which is the mass of the lesion, most often on the foot.
Without treatment the infection spreads along fascial planes into muscle and bone.

nodes.description: Mycetoma can spread beyond subcutaneous tissues to deeper structures, including bone, with osteolytic destruction in advanced cases.

evidence.snippet: Imaging showed a bone involvement with osteolysis at the levels of 2nd to 4th metatarsal diaphysis.

nodes.description: The host response is a neutrophil-rich suppurative reaction that matures into epithelioid granulomas around the organisms, with macrophages, plasma cells and lymphocytes. Histology shows three reaction types that reflect stages from acute to chronic infection.

evidence.reference_title: Mycetoma: Development of Diagnosis and Treatment.
evidence.snippet: the local-host reactions to the infections result in the formation of epithelioid granulomas with either fungi or bacteria inside and with surrounding acute and chronic inflammation.

evidence.reference_title: Mycetoma: Development of Diagnosis and Treatment.
evidence.snippet: Type I: The fungal elements are surrounded by a layer of neutrophils and then surrounded by plasma cells, macrophages, lymphocytes, neutrophils, eosinophils, and blood vessels, forming a granulomatous tissue

evidence.reference_title: Mycetoma: Development of Diagnosis and Treatment.
evidence.snippet: These three types of histological manifestations are not separated events but reflect the different stages of the pathogenesis from acute to chronic infection.

nodes.description: Mycetoma includes fungal (eumycetoma) and bacterial (actinomycetoma) infections.

evidence.reference_title: Mycetoma: Development of Diagnosis and Treatment.
evidence.snippet: Mycetoma describes a heterogeneous group of cutaneous and subcutaneous infections caused by either fungi (eumycetomas) or bacteria (actinomycetomas).

nodes.description: In late untreated disease organisms spread along fascial planes into muscle and bone, destroying and deforming osseous and muscular tissue.

evidence.reference_title: Mycetoma: Development of Diagnosis and Treatment.
evidence.snippet: In the late stage, the infection leads to the causative microorganisms spreading through the fascial planes to the underlying muscles and bones, and consequently, to the destruction and deformity of the osseous and muscular tissues and disfiguration.

nodes.description: Draining cutaneous sinus tracts are part of the classic clinical presentation of mycetoma lesions.

evidence.snippet: The clinical correlate of both forms of mycetoma is tumescence with abscesses, painless nodules, sinuses and discharge.

evidence.snippet: The prominent clinical presentation findings were multiple sinuses discharging grains (55%), massive swellings (46%), and lymphadenopathy (11.5%).

nodes.description: Mycetoma lesions commonly present as subcutaneous tumor-like swelling and predominantly affect the feet.

evidence.reference_title: Mycetoma: Development of Diagnosis and Treatment.
evidence.snippet: It is characterized by a triad of clinical symptoms: painless subcutaneous tumor-like swelling, multiple sinuses and fistulas, and discharged grains in pus. This predominantly affects the feet in more than 70% of patients.

nodes.description: Organisms in the tissue aggregate into grains, microcolonies encapsulated in a cement-like material with melanin that is believed to protect against host defences and antimicrobials. Grain colour, size and consistency differ by organism, and fungal and bacterial grains differ in biology.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical Features of Mycetoma and the Appropriate Treatment Options.
evidence.snippet: Grains which are seen in the discharge during the active phase of the disease, are the colonies of the causative microorganisms which are encapsulated in a cement-like material along with melanin and other substances.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical Features of Mycetoma and the Appropriate Treatment Options.
evidence.snippet: These coating materials are believed to protect against the host defense mechanisms as well the therapies with antimicrobials and antifungals.

nodes.description: Mycetoma discharge can contain visible grains, which are filamentous granules or microbial microcolonies in tissue.

evidence.reference_title: Eumycetoma and actinomycetoma--an update on causative agents, epidemiology, pathogenesis, diagnostics and therapy.

evidence.reference_title: An updated list of eumycetoma causative agents and their differences in grain formation and treatment response.
evidence.snippet: Clinically, no differences were reported in the appearance of the lesion, but variations in mycetoma grain formation and antifungal susceptibility were observed.

nodes.description: Itraconazole is a standard antifungal treatment for eumycetoma and served as the daily control arm in the Phase II fosravuconazole trial.

nodes.description: Madurella uses fungal sterol 14-alpha-demethylase in its ergosterol pathway. The CYP51/ERG11 enzyme activity is the Eumycetoma-local therapeutic vulnerability inhibited by itraconazole. This node represents normal enzyme activity; inhibition is encoded on the treatment edge.

evidence.snippet: The fungal cytochrome P450 enzyme sterol 14α-demethylase (SDM) is a key enzyme in the ergosterol biosynthesis pathway.
